data.name: Addal
data.gender_notes: Addal is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who serves, assists or supports. It is a name derived from the Arabic root 'ddl' which means to serve. The name implies strength, courage and a strong desire to help others. The name Addal carries the meaning “Servant, helper, support” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Addal usually hope their child will grow to embody servant, helper, support and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for those who are deeply committed to their faith and wish to serve their community in a meaningful way.
data.etymology: Addal belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Servant, helper, support.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Addal total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Addal" is a beautiful and significant name in Islamic culture, reflecting the religious and moral virtues of selflessness, generosity and service to others. In the Islamic faith, helping and serving others is considered a worthy act, reflecting the actions and values of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). The name Addal is therefore a reminder of this tradition and can instill a sense of social responsibility, compassion, and a strong work ethic.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Addal" also carries deep spiritual significance as it is a reminder of the importance of selflessness, humility, and serving the greater good. According to Islamic teachings, serving others is a form of worship and a means to please Allah, the Almighty. The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) is reported to have said, "The best amongst you are those who have the best manners and character. And it is better for a man to he above a man in position if he has better manners and character." (Sahih Muslim)

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah, vol. 7, p. 145 The name Addal carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Addal ibn Al-Aswad Al-Qurashi, also known as Al-Khidr, is mentioned in Surah Al-Kahf (18:65-82) as one of the two 'people of the unseen'. He was a pious servant of Allah, who traveled with Musa (Moses) and Al-Khidr. The story of Addal and Al-Khidr is an example of Allah's infinite wisdom and mercy.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Qurtubi's Jami' Al-Ahkam Al-Qur'an, vol. 13, p. 240 The name Addal carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Addal ibn Al-Fadl Al-Judhili, a companion of Prophet Muhammad, was one of the early converts to Islam. He was a poet and a scholar, and was known for his piety and devotion. He was given the epithet 'Addal' due to his extensive knowledge of the Quran and Hadith.
